problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+16y=4\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Second-Order Inhomogeneous ODEs With Sinusoidal Forcing

feedback.problem:
Find the general solutionto the problem

$$
{y}^{″}+16y=16\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+8\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
{y}^{″}+16y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-16\end{aligned}
$$

So $\lambda =\pm 4\text{i}$, and therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{c}(x)=A\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+B\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.
$$

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$

The particular solution of the inhomogeneous equation cannot be of the form $\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡4x$ because this is already included in the complementary function. Therefore, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡4x),
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & =(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡4x)+4x(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡4x) \\ {y}_{p}^{″} & =8(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡4x)+16x(-\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡4x-\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡4x).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

$$
8(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡4x)+16x(-\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡4x-\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡4x)+16x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡4x)\,=16\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+8\operatorname{sin}⁡4x
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
-8\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡4x+8\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡4x=16\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+8\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}8\beta =16\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡4x) \\ -8\alpha =8\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡4x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-1$ and $\beta =2.$ Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is:

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=x(-\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡4x)=-x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+2x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y={y}_{c}+{y}_{p}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+B\operatorname{sin}⁡4x-x\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+2x\operatorname{sin}⁡4x.
$$
